edition.en: The text follows the first printing, in The Crescent Moon (新月) 1:10, 10 December 1928, checked by Claude against the National Library of China scan of that issue on Wikimedia Commons. Written on 6 November 1928 on the China Sea. The book version in Fierce Tiger (猛虎集, 1931), which Wikisource transcribes from its 1932 reprint, differs in three small points: 上 for 生 in line 9, a comma after 滿載一船星輝, and no full stop after the date.
edition.zh: 文字依初刊本：1928 年 12 月 10 日《新月》月刊第一卷第十号，由 Claude 依维基共享资源所藏中国国家图书馆该期扫描核对。1928 年 11 月 6 日作于中国海上。维基文库据 1932 年再版本所录的《猛虎集》（1931）本与此有三处小异：第九行“生”作“上”，“满载一船星辉”后有逗号，末行日期后无句号。

basis.en: First published in December 1928 in The Crescent Moon, the printing followed here; the author died in 1931. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the poem was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1928 年 12 月初刊于《新月》，此处即依初刊本；作者卒于 1931 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: Written on a ship in the China Sea after Xu Zhimo’s last visit to Cambridge, where he had studied, this is probably the most recited modern Chinese poem. It is here because it says goodbye without grasping: the poet takes nothing away, not even a cloud. Notice the frame, softly in the first stanza and quietly in the last, and the moment in the middle when he wants to sing and cannot.
note.zh: 徐志摩最后一次重访他求学过的康桥之后，在中国海上的船中写成，这大概是被背诵得最多的一首现代汉语诗。收在这里，是因为它告别而不攫取：诗人什么也不带走，连一片云彩也不带走。留意首尾的“轻轻”与“悄悄”，以及中间那一刻，他想放歌，却不能放歌。

excerpt.orig: 我揮一揮衣袖，不帶走一片雲彩。
excerpt.en: I wave my sleeve and take away not a single cloud.
excerpt.zh: 我挥一挥衣袖，不带走一片云彩。

gloss.en: 輭 is an older form of 軟, soft. 生 is the reading of the 1928 printing, ‘grown from the soft mud’; the 1931 book has 上, ‘on the soft mud’.
gloss.zh: 原文“輭”，同“软”。“软泥生的”是 1928 年初刊本的文字；1931 年《猛虎集》本作“软泥上的”。

gloss.en: 荇 (xìng): floating heart, a water plant whose small round leaves lie on the surface; it is the 荇菜 of the first poem in the Book of Songs.
gloss.zh: 荇：荇菜，叶子浮在水面的水草，就是《诗经》首篇《关雎》“参差荇菜”的荇菜。

gloss.en: The Cam, the river that flows through Cambridge past the backs of the colleges.
gloss.zh: 康河：流经剑桥、从各学院后园穿过的河。

gloss.en: Usually identified as Byron’s Pool, upstream near Grantchester, said to have been a bathing place of the poet Byron; Xu mentions it in his essay ‘The Cambridge I Know’.
gloss.zh: 一般认为指上游格兰切斯特附近的拜伦潭，相传诗人拜伦常在那里游泳；徐志摩在散文《我所知道的康桥》里提到过它。

gloss.en: Punting: pushing a flat-bottomed boat along with a long pole, the Cambridge way of boating that Xu describes with delight in ‘The Cambridge I Know’.
gloss.zh: 撑长篙：撑篙行船，是康河上的玩法，徐志摩在《我所知道的康桥》里津津乐道地写过。

gloss.en: 溯 (sù): to go upstream; 漫溯, to drift upstream at leisure.
gloss.zh: 漫溯：随意地逆流而上。溯，逆流而行。

gloss.en: 笙 and 簫: the mouth organ and the end-blown bamboo flute, standing together for music.
gloss.zh: 笙箫：笙和箫，两种管乐器，合起来泛指音乐。

gloss.en: 康橋: Xu’s name for Cambridge, now usually written 劍橋. He studied there in 1921–22 at King’s College and came back for a short visit in the summer of 1928; this poem was written on the voyage home.
gloss.zh: 康桥：徐志摩对剑桥（Cambridge）的译名。他 1921 至 1922 年在剑桥大学国王学院学习，1928 年夏重访，这首诗写于回国的海上。
